Measured fields (electrical/thermal/duty) are null pending a fresh equilibrated capture; the 2026-07-19/20 run was a shakedown (see provenance). Fill measured values from that capture per schema.json.

identity.compressor_type: inverter, variable-speed (LG smart inverter; noted elsewhere as linear/BLDC — CONFIRM)
identity.control: adaptive defrost: initiates every 7-50 accumulated COMPRESSOR run-hours (service manual); ~3-min compressor lockout
identity.notes: nameplate_current_a (2.7 A) here is the WHOLE-UNIT RATED MAX at 115 V/60 Hz, not locked-rotor and not run current. Run current is compressor-class (~0.7 A). The 2.7 A ceiling is the basis for overcurrent_trip_a (set ~30% above it). Confirmed the unit never legitimately exceeds it in any mode incl. defrost (observed ~2.4 A defrost-entry peak sits just under).

factory_spec._comment: From the interior rating plate (photographed 2026-07-21). Not an EnerGuide/performance sticker; this is the nameplate.
factory_spec.notes: Defrost 198 W ~= 1.7 A @ 115 V, matching the observed ~1.9 A settled defrost draw. Icemaker heater line is blank (no icemaker heater load). See docs/todo.md P0 (confirmed root cause) for how these numbers closed the overnight-overcurrent diagnosis.

channel_binding.comment: As targeted by characterize_load.ino during the 2026-07-19/20 shakedown. 0-indexed array vs 1-indexed physical label is the recurring snare -- BOTH stated. Physical-socket identity NOT yet verified (open item).

waveform_crest_factor.confidence: high for the compressor as a LOWER BOUND; high for the heater
waveform_crest_factor.source: esp32_ads1115_cycle_stats, per-60Hz-cycle peak/RMS, 17.6h gap-free capture 2026-09-28/29 (fridgeCapture.txt). Compressor 2.657-2.728 across 16 separate runs; heater 1.44 mean over a full 29.6 min defrost.
waveform_crest_factor.notes:
NEW MEASUREMENT -- the rig cannot make it. A resistive reference (80W crock pot) on the same instrument reads 1.4125 against sqrt(2)=1.4142, so the heater at 1.41 is a textbook resistive load and the compressor at 2.68 is a rectifier-and-capacitor front end drawing current in short peaks near the voltage crest.

CORRECTION 2026-09-29 -- this field previously claimed the crest factor CORROBORATES the PF ~0.55 estimate, 'the same phenomenon seen two ways'. THAT WAS OVERSTATED. Crest factor constrains power factor only loosely: a load can draw peaky current and still be largely in phase. Combining this instrument's current with the Jackery's own wattmeter on the same load gives PF 0.76-0.89 across three readings (0.932A/100W, 0.938A/85W, 0.753A/70W at a measured 120V output), i.e. about 0.78 -- NOT 0.55. The ~0.55 on record looks too low and neither figure is a direct measurement. Settle it with a meter that reports PF directly, taking spot readings at each operating state, since these three suggest it VARIES with compressor load.

CREST FACTOR IDENTIFIES WHICH LOAD IS RUNNING, independent of current level -- compressor 2.68 vs heater 1.41 is unambiguous. A detection method the 1 Hz chain cannot do at all.

CAVEAT: the compressor figure is a LOWER BOUND. At ~14.7 samples per 60 Hz cycle a sine is sampled adequately (hence 1.4125 on the resistive check), but a waveform conducting for only part of each half-cycle puts few samples inside each current pulse. True crest factor is likely higher, and RMS may be slightly understated. A faster rate or a scope would be needed to pin it.

running_current_a.source: pre-event baseline of the 2026-07-19/20 shakedown current trace
running_current_a.notes: Variable-speed inverter: ~0.75 A steady near setpoint, but ~1.5 A during pulldown/recovery (box warm, e.g. post-defrost 2026-07-21). SUPERSEDE with settled values from the fresh capture.

inrush_peak_a.notes: WARNING: 10Hz/100ms-RMS sampling cannot resolve true inrush; any value is method-limited, not a surge peak.

plateau_a.notes: Inverter compressor: expect a smooth ramp, not a PTC shelf.

compressor_stop_profile._comment: Clean, heater-free compressor STOP (fridge's own cycle-end, power still applied). Isolates the inverter drive's deceleration profile -- the same rampdown seen inside the defrost entry (defrost.entry_transient), here with NO heater overlap to complicate it. Measured 2026-08-03 03:53 in data/run_auto_0802_1649.csv.
compressor_stop_profile.shape: STEPPED, not instant: ~747 mA running -> one intermediate speed plateau ~520 mA held ~4 s -> compressor out. The inverter drive steps the compressor through discrete speed setpoints; each is a flat current plateau (this is why the defrost-entry down-steps are flat, not a smooth decay).
compressor_stop_profile.detection_note: A compressor stop is a ~4-5 s event, not a single edge. Stop-detection must debounce ~4-5 s and NOT read the ~0.52 A intermediate plateau as a new steady state.

compressor_off_idle_a._comment: The fridge does NOT draw ~0 when its compressor is off -- while still powered it idles at ~120 mA / ~14 W (control board + inverter electronics, possibly a fan/damper). Held a median ~118 mA for minutes after the 08-03 03:53 stop, with relay_cmd=1 (power on) the whole time.
implications: 'compressor off' != 'zero current': set stop_a / compressor_on inference ABOVE ~120 mA and below ~750 mA running.
continuous between-cycle baseload to budget (~14 W), the fridge analog of the furnace ~12 W standby.
DISCRIMINATOR: a fridge-internal stop leaves the ~120 mA floor; OUR relay opening drops to true ~0 mA (power removed). The trace alone distinguishes 'the fridge chose to stop' from 'we cut it'.
compressor_off_idle_a.confidence: medium (single clean stop; value stable over ~4.5 min)

compressor_control_model._comment: REVERSE-ENGINEERED from current + FFC air-temp traces (NOT firmware). FACT (Ron 2026-08-11): the controller senses the FRESH-FOOD (FFC) temp ONLY -- not the freezer. The freezer swings widely as a side effect; the FFC damper is MANUAL (not an actuator). See memory fridge-controller-senses-ffc-only.
compressor_control_model.controlled_variable: FFC air temp (t2 column), ONLY. VERIFIED: at compressor ON/OFF edges the FFC value is ~3x tighter than the freezer value -- cut-out FFC std 0.18F vs frz 0.61F; cut-in FFC std 0.51F vs frz 1.69F (kitchen_fridge_run.csv 2026-07-19). An earlier freezer-thermostat reading was WRONG.
compressor_control_model.hypothesized_law: compressor_speed = Bias + Kp*e + Ki*integral(e), e = (FFC_temp - FFC_setpoint), Bias = LOAD-DEPENDENT feedforward. Current is a proxy for speed.

two_regimes.continuous_modulation: Higher load (e.g. Aug 2026): compressor runs continuously and MODULATES speed to hold FFC. Implied setpoint ~36.2F (asymptote midpoints, run_auto_0802).
two_regimes.on_off_cycling: Lower load (e.g. Jul 2026): the controller cannot hold FFC by modulation alone -- speed declines to the compressor MIN-SPEED FLOOR (~750 mA) and, with FFC still being over-cooled, CUTS OFF. FFC drifts up, then cuts back in. Same FFC loop, bang-bang outcome. ~30 min ON / ~18 min OFF.

compressor_control_model.ffc_thermostat_band_july: kitchen_fridge_run.csv 2026-07-19: cut-OUT at FFC ~38.9F (std 0.18), cut-IN at FFC ~40.1-40.5F (std 0.51). ~1.2-1.6F band, center ~39.5F. WARMER than the Aug ~36.2F -> the FFC dial was likely changed between captures; keep July vs Aug setpoints separate.
compressor_control_model.min_speed_floor_cutoff: CONFIRMED (Ron's observation). Within each ON period the current DECLINES (Kp*e shrinks as FFC cools) to a ~750-765 mA floor, and the compressor CUTS OFF while FFC is STILL COOLING -- FFC slope at cutoff -0.02 to -0.03 F/min on all 4 cycles. It cannot modulate below the floor, so once FFC hits the cut-out threshold it stops rather than over-cool.
compressor_control_model.identified_running_law_2026_08_11: MEASURED 2026-08-11 from kitchen_fridge_run.csv settled running cycles (2026-07-19/20, cycles B/C/D): while the compressor runs, current = 784 + 31*(FFC_temp - 39.5) mA (fit RMS ~17 mA, ~2%). i.e. Kp ~ 31 mA/F, and the same baseline (~784 mA at FFC 39.5 F) each settled cycle. The cut-off sits on the same line: at the cut-out FFC ~38.9 F the equation gives ~765 mA (the observed floor). The pulldown cycle A runs ~200 mA above this line (a higher baseline); the history before A is unknown -- the file is messy there -- so A's baseline is not pinned. Plot: analysis/ffc_control_law.png; see docs/lab_notebook.md 2026-08-11. CORRECTION of an earlier note here: it claimed the restart current fell across cycles because the box kept getting colder -- that was WRONG. The restart-current differences (873/839/814 mA) are just the FFC value at the moment of restart plus a brief startup surge; the settled cycles share one baseline.
compressor_control_model.droop_cancellation_hypothesis: SECONDARY / UNCERTAIN. In the continuous-modulation regime we saw sudden-onset speed RAMPS that re-target the FFC asymptote colder. One reading: detect near-stabilization at setpoint+offset, re-index the bias to setpoint-offset, ramp to it (event-triggered reset; size = table(setpoint-offset)-current_speed). BUT a blind scan did NOT confirm it generally: of 4 in-run ramps only 2 were preceded by a flattening; 2 fired while the box was actively warming or cooling hard. The hand-picked examples (08-05 03:05, 08-07 03:47) were SELECTION BIAS. So droop-cancellation may explain some ramps, not all in-run speed increases.

worked_example_asymptote_shift.ramp: current ~845 mA (flat) -> sudden onset ~03:47 -> ~912 mA over ~2.5 min
worked_example_asymptote_shift.fit_method: T(t) = Tinf + (T0-Tinf)*exp(-t/tau), numpy grid-search over tau. Pre: Tinf 36.9F, tau 15.6 min (well-constrained, ~1.7 tau). Post: Tinf 35.4F, tau 49.4 min (EXTRAPOLATED, ~0.75 tau before the reading went stale + compressor stopped). The 1.4F downward shift is robust; the exact post floor (35.4-36.0) is not.

compressor_control_model.ruled_out: (a) NOT freezer-controlled -- FFC is 3x tighter at the edges; Ron states FFC-only. (b) NOT a discrete speed 'step' for the in-run ramps -- fine data shows a ~2-3 min ramp, unlike the clean 100 ms edges at compressor stop. (c) NOT the FFC damper (it is MANUAL). (d) NOT simple integral windup (that gives no sudden onset).
compressor_control_model.caveats_and_open: HYPOTHESIS, not firmware-confirmed. We log FFC + freezer AIR temps and current only; internal controller state is unlogged. Kp, Ki, and the bias table are NOT yet numerically identified. OPEN: (1) fit Bias(load) from the cut-in restart current vs box temp across many cycles; (2) whether the sudden-onset ramps are clock-spaced (decision tick) or condition-tied -- early scan: intervals highly variable (12-268 min) -> NOT a fixed clock; (3) reconcile July(cycling ~39.5F)/Aug(continuous ~36.2F) setpoints = probable dial change.
compressor_control_model.confidence: FFC-only control HIGH; running law current=784+31*(FFC-39.5) mA and the cut-off floor data-backed for the 2026-07-19/20 settled cycles; the pulldown baseline and Ki NOT pinned; droop-cancellation LOW (blind scan did not confirm)
compressor_control_model.source: raw current + FFC air temp; kitchen_fridge_run.csv 2026-07-19 (cycling) + run_auto_0802_1649.csv 08-05/08-07 (continuous); model framing by Ron

control_constants.comment: Scale off MEASURED running_current_a, never nameplate. overcurrent trip is anchored to the 2.7 A whole-unit nameplate ceiling for this load.

start_confirm_a.basis: ~half of running current, above noise floor (~0.10A).

stop_a.basis: below run, above noise, below start_confirm for hysteresis.

start_debounce_ms.basis: sustained above start_confirm confirms real run vs stall.

max_offer_ms.basis: policy: satisfied box shows only noise -> release slot.

min_off_ms.basis: anti-short-cycle + ~3-min compressor cooldown/lockout, survives resets. Firmware startup hold-off AND overcurrent auto-retry both reuse this.

overcurrent_trip_a.basis: ~30% above the 2.7 A whole-unit nameplate max. Never trips on rated-normal operation (defrost ~2.4 A peak), still catches a genuine hard stall (much higher). Replaced the mis-scaled 1.5 A that false-tripped on defrost overnight. In characterize_load.ino.

overcurrent_trip_ms.basis: sustained-over debounce; ignores the brief defrost-entry peak and any startup inrush.

Freezer 0.418 F/min (~25 F/hr initial) matches the doc's ~0.3 F/min short-term estimate, but the curve TAPERS to ~3-4 F/hr over a multi-hour coast as it couples to the frozen mass. DO NOT extrapolate these to Part-B hours-scale coasts -- those must be measured directly. Per compartment.

measurement_2026_09_28.source: esp32_ads1115_cycle_stats at 60 windows/s, one complete defrost inside a 17.6h gap-free capture (fridgeCapture.txt), 2026-09-28/29.
measurement_2026_09_28.notes: CONFIRMS THE RECORDED STRUCTURE with measurements: heater 29.6 min, then a ~7.5 min dwell at 0.045A (everything off), then a 131 min recovery run at 94.9% duty. That is the '~30 min defrost + ~7 min dwell + pulldown-recovery' model in docs/todo.md, now measured end to end. Heater 1.696A/204VA against the recorded 1.8A/198W. Crest factor 1.44 during the heater period identifies it as purely resistive, so VA is essentially W.

dips_reexamined_2026_09_29.finding: The dips are REAL but were over-generalised. They occurred in ONE defrost of six examined, as two isolated single samples.
dips_reexamined_2026_09_29.source_file: run_20260721_135703.csv on the Ubuntu box -- a capture the provenance.capture_files list never recorded, which is why this took digging. Add it there.
dips_reexamined_2026_09_29.july_evidence: That file holds five defrosts. 07-21 14:24 (29.5 min, median 1.839A) contains two samples at exactly 1.000A, at t+15.8 and t+25.9 min -- 10.1 min apart, matching the original note exactly. The other four (07-22 13:55, 07-23 00:19, 07-23 13:58, 07-23 23:02) contain ZERO samples below 1.5A.
dips_reexamined_2026_09_29.september_evidence: The 2026-09-28 defrost at 60 windows/s: minimum 1.6377A, median 1.6969A, sd 0.0289A across 105838 windows of the 29.4 min heater period. Nothing below 1.5A. That is ~3500x the temporal resolution of the July chain, so a real heater interruption of even 17 ms would have been caught.
dips_reexamined_2026_09_29.on_the_value_1.000A: Checked as a possible code artifact; it is not. Values either side of 1.000A occur ~9000 times each in that file, so it is an ordinary reading.
dips_reexamined_2026_09_29.how_a_resistor_can_dip: It cannot on its own -- the control board would have to switch it. Each July dip is exactly ONE sample on a chain whose value updates every 1.05 s. A 100 ms RMS window straddling a heater switch-off reads an INTERMEDIATE value like 1.000A rather than zero, so the samples are consistent with a brief real interruption. They are equally consistent with two bad samples. One sample each cannot distinguish the two.
dips_reexamined_2026_09_29.dip_anatomy: Each dip is TEN ROWS at exactly 1.000A -- which is ONE underlying measurement, repeated ten times by dual_logger sample-and-hold. So the true event duration is UNKNOWN and bounded only by the Arduino 100ms RMS window; the apparent 1.0s is the logger, not the fridge. There is no within-dip variation to examine, because there is only one measurement. Dip 1 sits between neighbours of 1.832 and 1.842A; dip 2 between 1.838 and 1.846A.
dips_reexamined_2026_09_29.why_it_is_not_ordinary_noise: Consecutive distinct samples during normal heating vary by ~10mA (1.840, 1.832, 1.842, 1.837...). The dip differs from its neighbours by 840mA -- about 84x the sample-to-sample scatter.
dips_reexamined_2026_09_29.UNEXPLAINED -- exactly 1.000 twice: Every neighbouring sample carries three meaningful decimals; both dips are exactly 1.000. Checked whether 1.000 is an over-represented sentinel value in that file: it is NOT -- it occurs about as often as 0.997, 0.998 and 0.999, consistent with the compressor range passing through it. So no code path is obviously substituting a constant, and this is NOT resolved either way. Ron reads the three zeros as evidence of a digital rather than physical origin. The counter-arguments are that a sentinel would show a histogram spike and none exists, and that a DETERMINISTIC physical cause repeated twice would produce the same value twice -- identical events give identical measurements.
dips_reexamined_2026_09_29.if_real_the_arithmetic_fits: RMS 1.000 against a 1.839 baseline implies the heater was energised for (1.000/1.839)^2 = 30% of a 100ms window, i.e. roughly 30ms de-energised. That is a plausible duration for a board briefly cutting the heater to read the defrost thermistor.
dips_reexamined_2026_09_29.WHY IT STILL MATTERS DESPITE BEING RARE: The production controller will read the SAME ~1Hz chain that produced these samples. Whether the dip is physically real is irrelevant to it -- it sees the number. If that chain can emit 1.000 mid-defrost, detect-and-protect must not read it as defrost-over. The cost asymmetry is stark: a few seconds of software hysteresis against cutting the fridge at its WARMEST point, when docs/todo.md requires protecting a ~2.5h defrost-plus-recovery window and calls an interruption there a food-safety risk.
dips_reexamined_2026_09_29.consequence: Debounce defensively, but design nothing that DEPENDS on dips appearing, and read nothing into their absence. Frequency observed: 1 defrost in 6.

defrost._comment: Measured live during the 2026-07-21 fresh-capture power-up (provenance below). Triangulated: flat ~1.8 A resistive draw + compressor confirmed OFF (by observation) + melt water in the drain pan.
defrost.type: sensor-based adaptive (thermistor-terminated); NOT a fixed bimetal
defrost.duration_note: ~28-30 min (ended 2:54 PM 2026-07-21); exact value from the CSV (current step-up -> drop). This = the MIN UNINTERRUPTED WINDOW rotation must grant once a defrost is detected.
defrost.signature_note: flat ~1.8 A. CORRECTED 2026-09-29 -- this field previously described 'PERIODIC BRIEF DIPS to ~1 A (~15 & ~25 min in, ~10 min apart) = the board momentarily cutting the heater to sample the true coil temp', and required detect-and-protect logic to debounce them. THAT GENERALISED FROM n=2 IN A SINGLE DEFROST. See dips_reexamined_2026_09_29 under measurement_2026_09_28. Debouncing is still sound defensive practice, but nothing should DEPEND on dips appearing, and their absence means nothing.

entry_transient._comment: Current PROFILE at defrost ENTRY (the compressor->heater handoff). Measured from two independent defrosts; reproducible = a deterministic control sequence. Matches the service manual: 'Electrical parts such as COMP, defrost heater, freezer FAN, etc. operate in the following order to prevent noise and parts damage.'
entry_transient.shape: STAIRCASE, not a smooth curve: compressor running -> STEP UP to a ~2.4-2.6 A plateau (~2 s) -> STEP DOWN one plateau (~3-4 s) -> settles to heater-alone ~1.9 A. Plateaus are DEAD FLAT (no thermal decay within them) -> rules out a cold-element inrush. The down-steps are the COMPRESSOR DRIVE decelerating through discrete speed setpoints (confirmed by the clean heater-free stop, electrical.compressor_stop_profile: same ~4 s stepped rampdown), NOT the board relay-sequencing separate loads.
entry_transient.mechanism: At defrost initiation the board issues all commands ~simultaneously -- heater ON, evaporator fan OFF, compressor STOP (per the manual; the strict avoid-simultaneous ordering is really a START-UP behavior). But the heater is resistive (full-on in ms) while the compressor AND evap fan are BOTH BLDC (electronically driven, no relay-fast stop). So the compressor is still at full running current the instant the heater lands on top -> the ~2.6 A peak -> then its drive ramps it out over ~4-5 s. The overlap is a slow motor riding under an instant heater, NOT deliberate co-running (Ron, 2026-08-10). The small evap-fan term is buried in the first transition and can't be isolated from RMS current.
entry_transient.why_peak_below_scalar_sum: the peak (2.38-2.56 A) is BELOW 0.73/0.99 A comp + 1.9 A heater because RMS currents of the LAGGING compressor (motor, PF ~0.55) and the IN-PHASE heater (resistive) add as VECTORS, not arithmetically: |I| = sqrt(I_h^2 + I_c^2 + 2*I_h*I_c*cos(theta)). With heater 1.9 A, cos(theta) ~= 0.55 (theta ~57 deg) fits BOTH events. The peak scales with how hard the compressor is running at entry, at a ~constant 0.55 motor PF. CAVEAT: logger is RMS-amps only (no phase/PF); the 0.55 is INFERRED, to be confirmed by the scope's VA/PF measurement.
entry_transient.planning_note: Defrost ENTRY can hit ~2.6 A for ~2 s -- HIGHER than the flat ~1.9 A defrost steady. Small, but it is the real transient number for this load's worst brief draw.

measured_events.note: the event that tripped the OLD 1.5 A / 20 s latch (a false trip; threshold since rescaled to 3.5 A).

entry_transient.confidence: high on shape + reproducibility; medium on the inferred ~0.55 PF
entry_transient.source: raw 10 Hz current across two defrost entries; service manual sequencing note (Ron 2026-08-10)

post_defrost_peak_f.note: warmest point of the cycle; food-safe (freezer well under the 40 F ice-crystal line).

defrost.dwell_note: ~7 min from defrost end to compressor restart (drip/drain + anti-short-cycle). Normal. (Seen on the 1st defrost; the clean 2nd defrost went compressor-on almost immediately.)
defrost.pulldown_note: compressor restarts at ~1.0-1.4 A (inverter HIGH speed to recover the warm box), tapering toward ~0.8 A near setpoint. NB this sits near/above the OLD 1.5 A trip -> the 3.5 A rescale was needed for normal post-defrost recovery too, not just the heater.
defrost.recovery_note: MEASURED on the clean 2nd defrost (2026-07-22): after defrost end (freezer +17 F, peaked +22 F) the compressor ran CONTINUOUSLY ~2 h (14:26 -> first shutoff 16:26) to pull back to the -3.6 F cut-out; full return to steady ~0.8 A cycling took ~4.5 h. => PROTECTED WINDOW = defrost (~30 min) + recovery (~2 h) ~= 2.5 h during which rotation must NOT cut the fridge (box is at its warmest, un-recovered; cutting then risks food safety).
defrost.trigger: RESOLVED 2026-07-22 by SERVICE MANUAL + a 2nd observed defrost. Trigger is COMPRESSOR RUN-HOURS (not wall-clock, not power-on): manual says defrost fires between 7-50 accumulated compressor run-hours, ADAPTIVE by door-open time (more door-open -> more frost -> defrost nearer 7 h; undisturbed -> out toward 50 h). SPECIAL CASE: after a true power-on/restore, defrost at 4 run-hours (manual pt 2). Our data fits: 2nd defrost at ~13-14 run-hours (13:55-14:26, 30.4 min, ~1.87 A, mid-run, NO power cycle) is in-band; the immediate defrost on the 7/21 plug-in was an OVERDUE counter (the 3-min unplug did not reset run-hours -- carried a >50 h count from days on wall power), not a fresh power-on count.
defrost.duration: Manual pt 3: defrost TERMINATES when the evaporator defrost SENSOR reaches 10 C / 50 F (malfunction if not within 2 h). So duration is FROST-LOAD-DEPENDENT, not fixed. Both our defrosts ran ~30 min (29.0, 30.4) at moderate frost; heavier frost -> LONGER, up to a 2 h ceiling. Budget ~30 min typical, up to 2 h worst case. NB the 50 F is the evaporator sensor, not the freezer-air probe (freezer air only rose to ~+22-24 F during defrost).
defrost.adaptive_confirmed: 3 defrosts by 2026-07-23 confirm the manual's ADAPTIVE run-hour trigger FROM DATA. Integrated compressor run-hours between defrosts: 1st->2nd = 15.0 run-hours (quiet overnight, 65% duty, 23 h wall); 2nd->3rd = 8.0 run-hours (heavy dinner/evening door activity, 81% duty, 9.9 h wall). Threshold dropped 15->8 run-hours because door-open/frost pulled it toward the 7 h floor -- exactly 'defrost between 7-50 run-hours by door-open time'. Durations steady (~26, 30.4, 28.2 min). => DEFROST FREQUENCY TRACKS USE (door openings), not just run-hours.
defrost.budget_impact: Autonomous recurring defrost (~30 min typ / 198 W). Consequences: (1) run-hours basis means ROTATION STRETCHES the calendar interval (interrupted fridge accrues run-hours slower). (2) after a real outage/restore, defrost comes SOON (4 run-hours) -> budget it early in the first post-restore block. (3) MILD tailwind (do NOT bank it): defrost frequency scales with door-open activity, and outage door use is somewhat LOWER -- but the household still eats and cooks during outages, so assume only a MODEST reduction, not a large one (Ron, 2026-07-23). Our warm-bench doors-open testing is a slightly-worse-than-typical case, not a dramatic overestimate. Treat outage defrost frequency as ~similar to observed, maybe a bit less; do not rely on defrost being rare. (4) Effective duty for budgeting = steady cycling (~59%) PLUS periodic defrost+recovery overhead that scales with defrost frequency (the 65-81% interval duties include a ~2 h recovery run each).

deployment_2026_09_28.notes:
THE DECOMPOSITION IS THE POINT. Settled cycling is 46.9%; the whole 17.6h capture including one defrost and its 131 min recovery is 59.9%. The value_pct below (~59-60%, July night baseline) matches the WHOLE-CAPTURE figure almost exactly, which suggests that window contained a defrost too.

SO A DUTY FIGURE FOR THIS FRIDGE MEANS DIFFERENT THINGS depending on whether a defrost fell inside the window -- a 13-point swing. Defrost fires on accumulated compressor run-hours (7-50), so this is a scheduling term, not a constant, and docs/rotation_budget.md should carry both numbers rather than one.

Settled on/off (24.8/28.0) also differ from the July night baseline (~32/~21) in opposite directions -- shorter runs AND longer offs -- so conditions differed, not just defrost timing. Do not merge the two.
